item.text:
## 1B.9 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mostly precautionary and transparency-oriented** in the relevant domains. Lula’s government emphasized AI rights and information integrity, institutionalized digital-government transparency and secure data reuse, and kept cyber/critical-infrastructure policy grounded in risk management. I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of opaque or reckless handling in AI, cyber, bio, or other catastrophic-risk domains.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula publicly framed AI as something that should protect rights, data, and information integrity rather than amplify opaque power.
  - **Title:** [Speech by President Lula at the opening of the 79th UN General Assembly in New York](https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/speech-by-president-lula-at-the-opening-of-the-79th-un-general-assembly-in-new-york)
  - **Publisher:** Brazil G20 / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
  - **Date:** September 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/g20/en/documents/speeches/speech-by-president-lula-at-the-opening-of-the-79th-un-general-assembly-in-new-york
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said AI should be “a tool for peace, not war,” and that it should respect human rights, protect personal data, and promote information integrity. This is direct precaution/transparency evidence in a high-risk tech domain.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.9`; also `1B.1`, `1B.2`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s 2024 digital-government strategy explicitly tied technology use to transparency, secure reuse of data, participation, and a “trustworthy and secure” state.
  - **Title:** [Estratégia Nacional de Governo Digital](https://www.gov.br/governodigital/pt-br/estrategias-e-governanca-digital/estrategianacional/)
  - **Publisher:** Governo Digital / Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos
  - **Date:** 2024 framework page citing Decree No. 12.069 of June 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/governodigital/pt-br/estrategias-e-governanca-digital/estrategianacional/
  - **Claim-level summary:** The strategy says the 2024-2027 digital state should use technology appropriately, reuse data securely, expand transparency, and strengthen privacy/security. That is strong evidence of precaution and disclosure in a dual-use-adjacent domain.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.9`; also `1B.7`, `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s cyber policy in 2024 emphasized risk prevention, resilience, cooperation, and incident management.
  - **Title:** [Políticas Públicas](https://www.gov.br/anatel/pt-br/assuntos/seguranca-cibernetica/politicas-publicas)
  - **Publisher:** Anatel
  - **Date:** April 26, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/anatel/pt-br/assuntos/seguranca-cibernetica/politicas-publicas
  - **Claim-level summary:** The page describes Brazil’s national cyber policy as based on sovereignty, fundamental rights, incident prevention, resilience, education, and multistakeholder cooperation; it also notes the CNCiber was already operational in 2024. This is solid precautionary governance evidence for cyber-risk management.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.9`; also `1B.7`, `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Lula’s government paired climate-risk action with technical governance rather than purely political messaging.
  - **Title:** [Lula announces creation of climate authority](https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/lula-anuncia-criacao-de-autoridade-climatica)
  - **Publisher:** Brazil Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
  - **Date:** September 10, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/lula-anuncia-criacao-de-autoridade-climatica
  - **Claim-level summary:** The ministry said Lula announced a Climate Authority and a technical-scientific committee to coordinate responses to extreme events. Climate is not cyber or bio, but it is an “other catastrophic-risk domain,” and the policy choice is precautionary and institutional.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.9`; also `4A`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s biological-risk governance framework continued to emphasize safety norms, inspection, and precaution.
  - **Title:** [Lei nº 11.105 de 24/03/2005](https://www.gov.br/mdic/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/institucional/atos-normativos/leis/lei-no-11-105-de-24-de-marco-de-2005)
  - **Publisher:** Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços
  - **Date:** Updated January 25, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/mdic/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/institucional/atos-normativos/leis/lei-no-11-105-de-24-de-marco-de-2005
  - **Claim-level summary:** The official text highlights safety norms, inspection mechanisms, and the principle of precaution for GMO-related activities. This is background, not a Lula-initiated 2024 reform, but it is still relevant to how Brazil handled biological dual-use-adjacent governance.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.9`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula:
- pushed dual-use tech without safeguards,
- hid cyber or AI risk decisions from public review,
- weakened biosafety or cyber controls,
- or used a catastrophic-risk domain to concentrate power.

The available evidence is mostly the opposite: transparent digital governance, explicit AI rights language, precautionary cyber policy, and technical committees for climate risk.
